problems.what: the rule itself: ask for capacity, not content
problems.replace: if it requires you to destabilize to know it!
problems.with: if it requires you to destabilize to know it! Ask for capacity, not content.

problems.what: something the conscious mind can't yet tolerate
problems.replace: that it is difficult for your conscious mind to know
problems.with: that your conscious mind can’t handle yet

problems.what: regulation and support come before deeper dialogue; silence may be protection while the adult lacks the capacity (not 'it is not good for your subconscious to communicate', 'silence is safer')
problems.replace: Until your adult has enough of these capacities, especially regulation and support, it is not good for your subconscious to communicate with you. Silence is safer.
problems.with: In that state, regulation and support come before going deeper. The silence may be protecting you while your adult doesn’t have enough regulation, support, humility or practical capacity to take it in.

problems.what: the first question: content now, or capacity first?
problems.replace: “What do you need for my conscious mind
problems.with: “Do I need to know the content now, or do I need to build capacity first?” “What do you need for my conscious mind

problems.what: become someone who can know it safely; preparation before revelation, grounding before memory, support before intensity; one next action
problems.replace: Please prepare me to hear it in a way that is safe. Ground me. Get me support. Tell me what to do.”
problems.with: Help me become someone who can know it safely. Prepare me before you reveal it, ground me before the memory, support me before the intensity. Give me one next thing to do.”

problems.what: imagery can be meaningful without being literal; the mind symbolizes, compresses, distorts, dramatizes and borrows from culture and fear; treat an image as an image and get outside support when needed
problems.replace: REMEMBER: Hypnotic imagery is not always literal, especially around trauma and memory.
problems.with: REMEMBER: Hypnotic imagery can mean something without being literal, especially around trauma and memory. The mind turns things into symbols, squashes them together, distorts and dramatizes them, and borrows from culture and fear. Treat an image as an image, and get outside support when you need it.
